The Risk of Budget Overruns and the Pitfalls of Ambiguous Per-Square-Meter Quotes

Building a house is one of the most significant financial decisions in a person's life, requiring years of savings and extremely careful cash-flow planning. Yet current conditions in Central Vietnam show that more than 80% of homeowners experience severe financial stress, exhaust their available funds, or are forced to halt construction before completion because actual costs far exceed the original estimate. The primary cause is not construction-material inflation, but the trap of ambiguous floor-area pricing offered by underqualified contractors. They submit an attractively low total bid to secure the contract, then add hidden charges for essential work once foundation excavation begins. Understanding every component of turnkey house construction costs in Da Nang from a professional perspective provides crucial protection, enabling you to manage the budget and maintain control of cash flow from groundbreaking through handover.

1. Initial Administrative and Legal Costs, Site Surveying, and Boundary Verification

The first item, and the legal foundation for the entire project, is administrative and legal expenditure, which homeowners often overlook in contingency budgets. This covers fees for preparing architectural and structural drawings and technical documentation for submission to the relevant authorities to obtain an urban construction permit in compliance with regulations. Mandatory on-site work also includes commissioning a survey of existing site conditions and setting out foundation centerlines with a high-precision total station to establish the boundaries recorded on the land-use certificate and prevent encroachment on adjoining properties. When clients choose MVN Group's end-to-end service, our specialists handle the complex administrative procedures at the district one-stop office, giving busy homeowners complete peace of mind.

2. Structural Shell Construction Costs – The Building's Permanent Load-Bearing Framework

The structural shell is the building's principal load-bearing framework, determining its long-term durability and safety under the severe storms and floods of Central Vietnam. This major component is fixed within the total turnkey construction cost in Da Nang and includes structural materials and labor. MVN Group applies strict specifications for primary materials: genuine Hòa Phát CB300/CB400 deformed reinforcing steel; Kim Đỉnh or Cẩm Phả cement compliant with PCB40 standards; grade-1 Đại Hiệp fired-clay bricks with straight, sharp edges; coarse aggregate sand for casting concrete beams and columns; and screened medium-grain sand free of organic impurities for grade-75 masonry and plastering mortar. High-strength M250/M300 ready-mix concrete used for foundation caps, columns, primary beams, and secondary beams undergoes an Abram cone slump test (10±2cm) and rigorous compressive-strength testing of cast cube samples to ensure maximum structural performance.

3. Architectural Finishes – The Area Most Likely to Cause Budget Overruns

While structural shell costs can be quantified from fixed geometric quantities, finish selections create a complex pricing landscape and present the greatest risk of exceeding the homeowner's budget. This category encompasses all materials outside the load-bearing structure that directly define the home's aesthetic quality and standard of living. It includes semi-porcelain granite floor and wall tiles with high wear resistance; sanitary fixtures (Toto, Inax); alkali-resistant interior and exterior paints (Dulux, Jotun); premium exterior aluminum and tempered-glass door systems with weather-tight seals; Flat concealed-frame gypsum ceilings by Vĩnh Tường; and LED lighting. To protect clients' finances, MVN Group clearly categorizes finishes into Standard, Enhanced, and Premium material packages in the contract appendix. All technical specifications, color codes, and brands are fixed, with the contractor assuming the risk of market price fluctuations.

4. Concealed Mechanical and Electrical (M&E) System Installation to Prevent Overloads and Short Circuits

The concealed mechanical, electrical, and plumbing network (M&E) functions as the building's circulatory system, supporting the family's long-term comfort. Costs include rigid fire-resistant electrical conduit, heavy-gauge insulated copper cable by Cadivi, and heat-resistant high-pressure PPR water-supply and drainage pipes joined by leak-resistant heat fusion. In a contemporary townhouse designed in 2026, M&E engineers must coordinate the building-services layout with the load-bearing structural drawings before casting beams and floor slabs. This prevents later drilling or cutting through cured beams and columns, which would compromise structural capacity. All cable junctions and service boxes are logically positioned to support long-term maintenance.

5. Site Management and Supervision, Scaffolding and Protective Enclosures, and Post-Construction Cleaning

The final component of a turnkey construction budget covers coordination and operational management on site. It funds regional lead engineers and the site manager, who provide 24/7 oversight, monitor the schedule in MS Project, and conduct staged technical inspections with the homeowner. It also covers temporary worker facilities; protective sheeting for moist-curing concrete; safe, fully enclosed scaffolding with dense netting to prevent falling materials and avoid settlement or cracking in adjoining party walls; and professional post-construction cleaning before key handover. Incorporating all these supporting items into the turnkey contract gives homeowners complete peace of mind without having to manage minor daily expenses.
